text:
**Short answer: yes, at about $450-$500 or less, if you mainly run AC loads. Below that tier, newer alternatives may beat it.**

**Why it's worth it**
- **Real capacity is good.** Six independent tests measured 82-90% of the rated 1,152 Wh, about 991 Wh at the median ([Watt Power Station](https://wattpowerstation.com/power-stations/bluetti-ac180/)). PCWorld got 970-1,007 Wh on AC loads and called its AC efficiency class-leading ([PCWorld](https://www.pcworld.com/article/1966571/bluetti-ac180-power-station-review.html)).
- **Power and durability.** It puts out 1,800 W continuous (2,700 W surge), uses a LiFePO4 battery rated for 3,500+ cycles, and has a 5-year warranty. It fully recharges in about 1.3-1.8 hours in Turbo mode ([OutdoorGearLab](https://www.outdoorgearlab.com/reviews/camping-and-hiking/power-station/bluetti-ac180)).
- **Price.** It's $499 at Bluetti and about $449 on Amazon, which works out to roughly $0.45 per usable Wh ([iTechGuides](https://www.itechguides.com/bluetti-ac180-power-station-review-excellent-ac-efficiency-but-heavy-and-less-impressive-over-dc/)).

**Drawbacks**
- **Heavy for its capacity.** It weighs about 36 lb. OutdoorGearLab scored it 66 overall and noted a noisy fan and a poor power-to-weight ratio.
- **Weak on small loads.** At a ~34 W draw (CPAP, fridge overnight), one test got only 54% of rated capacity ([Watt Power Station](https://wattpowerstation.com/power-stations/bluetti-ac180/)).
- **Weak on DC.** PCWorld measured only 71% efficiency on a USB-PD load ([iTechGuides](https://www.itechguides.com/bluetti-ac180-power-station-review-excellent-ac-efficiency-but-heavy-and-less-impressive-over-dc/)).
- **Expansion is limited.** Sources disagree. Bluetti markets expansion batteries, but the Dealectric listing says it has no expansion port and can only be topped up from a B80/B230/B300 in Power Bank Mode, and Watt Power Station calls it not expandable. Don't buy it planning to scale up.
- **Heat and UPS caveats.** Output drops to 1,500 W above 95°F. The app's Grid Enhancement mode can break the UPS backup function ([Best Batteries](https://us.best-batteries.com/reviews/bluetti-ac180/)).
- **Possibly being phased out.** OutdoorGearLab says the newer Bluetti Elite 100 v2 is a better product: lighter (25 lb), quieter, faster charging, and cheaper, with 1,024 Wh. It also prefers the Anker Solix C1000 Gen 2, which it says costs less and delivers more. Both are in the $489-$500 range on Watt Power Station's comparison. I don't have purchase links for them in these results.

**Who should buy it:** people who want a well-tested 1 kWh unit for outages, power tools, and weekend camping, and who run mostly AC loads.

**Who should skip it:** anyone who needs a lighter unit, wants to expand later, or runs mostly low-wattage or USB loads. Compare the Elite 100 v2 and Anker C1000 Gen 2 first.

**Where to buy**
- [BLUETTI official US store, $499 (5-year warranty, 30-day returns)](https://www.bluettipower.com/products/ac180?variant=44099774480603)
- Dealectric tested code AFF5OFF for $24.95 off, bringing it to $474.05. It's an [affiliate link](https://dealectric.com/go/bluetti-ac180) that pays them a commission and doesn't cost you more. Checkout has the final word on price.
- An Amazon listing showed $449, but I don't have a direct link from these results. Check that it's the standalone AC180 and not a bundle.
